newsitem.title: UK: Police chief warns of IRA pre-Christmas attacks.
newsitem.headline: Police chief warns of IRA pre-Christmas attacks.

text.p: London's chief of police on Thursday said the Irish Republican Army (IRA) could be planning pre-Christmas attacks on shopping centres in the British capital.

Metropolitan Police Commissioner Paul Condon said the IRA had a history of launching attacks against shoppers crowding into the city before Christmas, seeing it as a prime time to publicise their cause.

The IRA traditionally declares a short ceasefire over Christmas but republican sources have ruled out the truce this year after Prime Minister John Major effectively refused to make concessions to the IRA's political arm Sinn Fein.
Condon said his force was on alert for assassinations, bomb attacks and firebombings and urged Londoners to keep an eye out for any suspicious activity.
"It's by making London as hostile an environment as possible for the IRA to operate in that gives us the best chance of success," he told reporters.
The IRA abandoned a 17-month ceasefire in February and detonated a huge device in eastern London in the first of a series of bombings on the mainland to press its campaign for a united Ireland.
Its last successful bombing was on Britain's main army barracks in Northern Ireland in October.
